title: EU AML Regulation (AMLR) for payment and e-money institutions | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: What the EU AMLR means for payment and e-money institutions: CDD thresholds, the e-money exemption, linked remittances, eIDs and the EUDI Wallet.
body_markdown:
*What the EU AMLR and AMLA’s final draft standards mean for onboarding, occasional transfers, e-money products and remote identification.*


Payment institutions and electronic money institutions are obliged entities under the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR), which applies directly from 10 July 2027. They must apply customer due diligence when they establish a business relationship, when they carry out an occasional transaction of EUR 10,000 or more, and when they initiate or execute an occasional transfer of funds of EUR 1,000 or more, in a single operation or through linked transactions. Under AMLA’s final draft standards, remote verification is expected to use suitable eIDs, including the EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet), or relevant qualified trust services wherever possible.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Ivan Mikić (International Sales Director), Authologic.*
